newsitem.title: USA: Record bidding in U.S. Gulf Texas lease sale.
newsitem.headline: Record bidding in U.S. Gulf Texas lease sale.

text.p: A record number of bids were submitted for leases on exploration and production rights in the western Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday, the U.S. Minerals Management Service said.

The agency, which regulates drilling in federal waters of the Gulf, said 929 bids to explore for oil and natural gas were submitted on 617 tracts off the coasts of Texas and western Louisiana. The winning bids totalled $352.5 million.
"That's a pretty strong western sale," said Chris Oynes, regional director of the federal agency.
Held in a packed hotel ballroom in New Orleans' French Quarter, the lease sale was the first in which royalty relief was available on deepwater production in the western Gulf.

As expected, the most active bidding was in the Garden Banks section of the Gulf southeast of Sabine Pass, and intense bidding emerged for some deepwater tracts in the Alaminos Canyon area east of Corpus Christi, Texas.

One of the most aggressive bidders to emerge in the sealed- bid auction was Barrett Resources, which posted the lease round's high bid of $13 million on a tract in the High Island section of the Gulf, topping the nearest bidder by nearly $10 million for rights to that block.

A bidding war of sorts erupted in the Alaminos Canyon area, where several producers clustered bids in two groups of blocks. "When you see multiple interest like that, everybody's got a seismic (survey) that shows a bright spot," an indication of possible hydrocarbons, said Blake Wright, an analyst tracking Gulf drilling for Offshore Data Services.
